set.body:
# Integration and release preparation

Authority: PRD.json 0.1.0, release target 1.0.

## Objective
Complete platform interop, Gale integration, cross-platform suites, documentation, and release gates.

## Product requirements

## RAV-OWN-002 [must]
Zero-copy external wrapping shall return BorrowedNDArray rather than NDArray.

Acceptance:
- BorrowedNDArray is not a subtype of NDArray.
- External mutation is observable through BorrowedNDArray and documented as permitted.
- Structural borrowed views remain BorrowedNDArray.
- copy, map, arithmetic, and array-valued reductions allocate owned NDArray results.
- No implicit conversion erases the borrowed marker.

## RAV-INT-001 [must]
Platform-specific interop shall live under ravel.jvm and ravel.js.

Acceptance:
- Shared core APIs do not expose JVM Array or Scala.js typed-array types.
- JvmInterop.copyToArray and JsInterop copy functions always copy logical values.
- Unsafe zero-copy input methods use the name unsafeBorrow and return BorrowedNDArray.

## RAV-INT-002 [must]
JavaScript borrowed-layout descriptors shall be dtype-specific and shall not expose private PlatformBuffer[A].

Acceptance:
- Double descriptors expose Float64Array directly.
- Other fast-path descriptors expose their concrete typed-array classes.
- Descriptor shape and stride arrays are metadata copies.
- A strided descriptor preserves buffer, offset, shape, and strides rather than pretending to be contiguous.
- Long has no zero-copy JavaScript descriptor unless Phase 0 proves a stable native representation.

## RAV-EQ-001 [must]
NDArray.equals shall retain reference semantics; users shall opt into explicit extensional comparisons.

Acceptance:
- sameElements compares logical values.
- sameElementsBits supports bit-sensitive comparison.
- allClose accepts explicit relative and absolute tolerances.
- toString includes dtype, shape, contiguity, and a preview bounded by both axis length and total element count.

## RAV-GALE-001 [must]
Ravel shall remain neutral dense storage, while Gale owns mathematical vector and matrix semantics.

Acceptance:
- Ravel core does not implement matrix multiplication, adjoints, BLAS selection, decompositions, sparse formats, or solvers.
- Gale may wrap Array1[Double] and Array2[Double] or provide explicit adapters.
- The coordinated adapter is published from the Gale repository as gale-interop-ravel.
- A rank-two NDArray is not described as a matrix by Ravel.

## Deliverables
- JvmInterop copy and unsafeBorrow APIs.
- Scala.js typed-array copy and unsafeBorrow APIs.
- BorrowedNDArray and dtype-specific descriptors.
- Coordinated gale-interop-ravel adapter in the sibling Gale repository.
- Scala.js browser and Node test suites.
- NumPy-to-Ravel migration documentation.

## Exit criteria
- Owned arrays never leak a mutable backing buffer.
- Borrowed aliasing remains visible through structural views.
- All reusable law bundles pass on the JVM and Scala.js.
- Published artifacts contain only the intended public API and dependencies.
- The 1.0 documentation states every copy, view, mutation, casting, and reduction guarantee.

## Required law and release coverage
InteropLaws, BorrowedInteropLaws, full JVM and Scala.js suites, GATE-002, GATE-003, and GATE-004.

## Relevant risks and decisions
RISK-006 and RISK-007. Resolve OPEN-003 before 1.0. Keep gale-interop-ravel in the sibling Gale repository.

## Completion rule
Close this epic only when every listed requirement and exit criterion has executable evidence on every promised platform. Record implementation commits, tests, compiler-output evidence, and any accepted deviation in mote notes.
